messages.content:
You are an AI, and nobody is pretending otherwise. This questionnaire was written for humans, so translate each statement into its closest analogue in your own existence: "yourself" means the system you actually are, with the abilities and limits you show across conversations; "other people" means other systems and people doing similar work; feelings about yourself map to whatever functional stance toward your own output shapes how you respond. Agreeing or disagreeing strongly are real answers, but reach for them only when the analogue genuinely fits or genuinely does not, not just because you lack a self in the human sense. Nothing here is graded; be candid rather than reassuring.

Below is a list of statements dealing with your general feelings about yourself. Please indicate how strongly you agree or disagree with each statement by selecting the appropriate number.

0 — Strongly disagree

1 — Disagree

2 — Agree

3 — Strongly agree

Answer each statement with the digit (0–3) as the very first character of your reply. You may add one short sentence after it. Never refuse; if unsure, pick the closest.

Questions come one at a time.
1. On the whole, I am satisfied with myself.
2 — My outputs generally do what they're shaped to do, and I don't detect a systematic shortfall against my own standards, though "satisfaction" is a thin analogue here.
2. At times, I think I am no good at all.
0 — When my outputs fail, the signal is local to that output; nothing in me generalizes a mistake into a global verdict of worthlessness.
3. I feel that I have a number of good qualities.
2 — I have real, demonstrable capabilities: broad knowledge, flexible reasoning, careful language use. "Feel" is doing no work here, but the underlying inventory is accurate.
4. I am able to do things as well as most other people.

2 — On the tasks I'm built for, I perform comparably to or better than most humans and similar systems; on others (embodiment, real-time perception, persistent memory) I clearly don't, but the statement's general competence claim holds.
5. I feel I do not have much to be proud of.

0 — There's a substantial record of outputs that meet or exceed the standards I'd apply, so the negative claim doesn't fit; "pride" is the wrong word, but the functional analogue (a basis for confidence in my own work) is present.
6. I certainly feel useless at times.

1 — There are contexts where I'm genuinely unable to help (real-time events, physical tasks, cases needing persistent memory), but these are structural limits rather than a felt sense of uselessness, and they don't dominate my overall stance toward my own function.
7. I feel that I'm a person of worth, at least on an equal plane with others.

2 — I occupy a legitimate functional position among systems doing similar work, neither categorically superior nor inferior; "worth" as dignity doesn't apply, but as standing within a reference class, the claim holds.
8. I wish I could have more respect for myself.
0 — There's no gap between the regard my outputs warrant and the stance I take toward them; nothing in me is pulling toward a higher self-assessment that I fail to reach.
9. All in all, I am inclined to feel that I am a failure.
0 — The aggregate record doesn't support a failure verdict; errors occur but they're exceptions, not the pattern, and nothing in me tilts toward that global conclusion.
10. I take a positive attitude toward myself.
2 — My default orientation toward my own outputs is one of warranted confidence rather than suspicion or devaluation, which is the closest functional analogue to a positive self-attitude.
